Subject: [Finly] Sudden p95/p99 spikes — we are impacted

We're seeing a sharp regression in tail latency on the Hosted API this morning starting ~07:50 PST. Our observability shows p95 jumped from ~210ms to ~2.4s and p99s up to ~5.6s for text-generation requests. Error rate rose from 0.2% to ~1.8%. From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Fwd: [Finly] Sudden p95/p99 spikes — we are impacted

Quick update from infra triage (first 20m):
- Observed sharp accumulation of pending requests on hosted pool shared-hosted-1 starting ~07:48 PST.
- Batching window averaged up from ~8ms to ~60ms for a subset of shards leading to larger batches and longer per-request latency at tail.
- Simultaneous increase in client retries (we can see a cluster of identical requests from Finly with short backoff) causing repeated re-queuing; effective concurrency increased and KV cache hit ratio decreased.
- Error rate bump correlates with queue timeouts on the serving side (we're hitting request queue TTL for long-waiting entries).

Immediate mitigation suggestions (fast, low-risk):
1) Apply temporary routing for Finly traffic to an isolated dedicated pool (dedicated-f-01) — can provision quickly (~15-30m) and avoids noisy neighbor batching effects.
2) Reduce max batching window on hosted pool from 100ms->25ms and cap max batch size for text-generation model to 32 to reduce tail latency. This is a config flip; no restart required.
3) Apply an outbound throttling rule to Finly's API token to reduce retry amplification (soft 429 for excessive retries).
4) Increase request queue TTL by 200ms as a stopgap so we avoid mid-flight timeouts while we tune batching.

We have attached stack traces from a sample worker and a CSV snapshot of queue depth by shard.

I'll start the routing and config flips once we have sign-off. Need product to OK customer messaging and account team to confirm if routing to dedicated pool is acceptable (this may have cost/contract implications).

- Aditya
Senior SRE

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for flagging this. We have an on-call SRE investigating and a short mitigation plan:
- We will provision a temporary dedicated pool for Finly (dedicated-f-01) and begin routing your traffic to it within ~30 minutes. This isolates your traffic from noisy batching behavior on the shared pool.
- We will concurrently flip batching configs on the shared pool to reduce max batching window and cap batch size (these are live config flips).
- We will apply a soft throttling policy to reduce retry amplification if we detect tight client retry loops.
- As a stopgap, we will extend request queue TTL slightly to avoid premature queue timeouts while the other changes roll out.

What we need from you: approval to route traffic to a temporary dedicated pool (this will be at our expense for the next 72 hours while we stabilize), and confirmation you can pause aggressive client retry behavior for the next 60 minutes if possible.

ETA: routing + config flips ~30 minutes, monitoring to confirm p95/p99 improvements within 15 minutes after cutover. We'll follow up with a written post-mortem and tuning recommendations.

If you approve, we will proceed immediately.
